description: Hand-written: the progression.* and skill.* rows’ own contract (PL.native-progression-rows, U106(7); core’s P9i progression and skill trees) — each row’s answer over core’s function, the run one tracker step answers being the run the next is sent, core’s refusals as VALUES (an unknown step kind, a bad date, an unknown award, an unreadable save block, an unknown node), the rows’ own refusals as errors coded [invalid-input], an unknown row refused by the method table, and the skill session: each SkillProgression method with the events core raised, the no-KB rule (a node that asks anything stays locked until a world’s rules open it) and, on the C leg, a KB-backed unlock answered by core’s skill_goal_met/2. Every expectation here was computed by core’s own functions at the pin, not by these rows. Core’s own corpora (conformance/progression/*.json, conformance/skills/*.json and the can_unlock cases of conformance/prolog/mechanic-skill.json) are driven whole through these rows by the progression_corpus ctest (tests/progression_corpus.cpp), not transcribed here.

cases.name: progression.gamification: each row is one of core’s tracker functions; the run one step answers is the run the next step is sent; a refused step (an unknown step kind, a bad date, an unknown award or bus event) is core’s refusal as a VALUE
progression.* and skill.*: the rows’ own refusals are errors coded [invalid-input]; a session nobody opened is refused

cases.name: skill session WITH a KB: skill.unlock asks core’s skill_goal_met/2 in the native KB (U106(7)); one guild member’s standing opens the node for that member only, a take’s facts are written to the KB (the node below it opens only after, and a goal on the points sees the new count, the old one retracted), and a KB the engine refuses is [invalid-input]
cases.why: the KB is a native Prolog KB, and the JS harness has no Prolog engine

kb: skill_capped(A, S) :- has_skill(A, S, L), skill_max_level(S, L).
can_learn_skill(A, S) :- skill_defined(S, _), \+ has_skill(A, S, _), \+ (skill_requires(S, P, Min), \+ (has_skill(A, P, L), L >= Min)).
can_advance(A, S) :- has_skill(A, S, L), \+ skill_capped(A, S), Next is L + 1, skill_level_xp(S, Next, Need), skill_xp(A, S, X), X >= Need.
skill_goal_met(A, Goal) :- Goal =.. [F, _ | Rest], Bound =.. [F, A | Rest], call(Bound).
skill_points_held(A, T, P) :- skill_points(A, T, P), !.
can_unlock(A, N) :- skill_node(N, T), \+ skill_unlocked(A, N), skill_node_price(N, C), skill_points_held(A, T, P), P >= C, \+ (skill_node_requires(N, G), \+ skill_goal_met(A, G)).
skill_effect(A, E) :- skill_unlocked(A, N), skill_node_effect(N, E).
guild_standing(A, G, Min) :- reputation(A, G, R), R >= Min.
